title: Inflation between finite cyclic groups
statement: For $m\geq1$ let $C_m=\langle\sigma\rangle$ be cyclic of order $m$ and $N_m=1+\sigma+\dots+\sigma^{m-1}\in\mathbf Z[C_m]$. Let $r\geq1$, let $\pi\colon C_{rm}\to C_m$ send a generator $\sigma'$ to $\sigma$, and let $M$ be an abelian group with a $C_m$-action by group automorphisms (a $C_m$-module), regarded as a $C_{rm}$-module through $\pi$. For every integer $s\geq0$, the inflation map $H^s(C_m,M)\to H^s(C_{rm},M)$ is multiplication by $r^{\lfloor s/2\rfloor}$ under the identifications of the source with the cohomology of the periodic complex $M\xrightarrow{\sigma-1}M\xrightarrow{N_m}M\xrightarrow{\sigma-1}\cdots$ and the target with the cohomology of $M\xrightarrow{\sigma-1}M\xrightarrow{rN_m}M\xrightarrow{\sigma-1}\cdots$. Here the scalar description means that the cohomology class represented by $x$ is sent to the class represented by $r^{\lfloor s/2\rfloor}x$ in the target complex. Group cohomology $H^s(G,M)$ is the cohomology of the inhomogeneous group-cochain complex of functions $G^q\to M$, with differential $(da)(g_1,\ldots,g_{q+1})=g_1a(g_2,\ldots,g_{q+1})+\sum_{j=1}^{q}(-1)^j a(g_1,\ldots,g_jg_{j+1},\ldots,g_{q+1})+(-1)^{q+1}a(g_1,\ldots,g_q)$; inflation is the map induced by pulling these functions back along $\pi$ in every argument. In particular, if $rM=0$, inflation is zero in all degrees $s\geq2$.

proof.text: For each positive integer $n$, [lem-sfb-cyclic-periodic-resolution] gives the free periodic resolution of the trivial $\mathbf Z[C_n]$-module and identifies the cochain complex computing $H^s(C_n,M)$ with alternating maps $\sigma-1$ and $N_n$. For $n=m$ this is $M\xrightarrow{\sigma-1}M\xrightarrow{N_m}M\to\cdots$; for $n=rm$, the action of $\sigma'$ on $M$ is the action of $\sigma$, while the norm is $N_{rm}$ acting through $\pi$, namely $\sum_{a=0}^{r-1}\sum_{b=0}^{m-1}\sigma^{am+b}=rN_m$, so the target complex is $M\xrightarrow{\sigma-1}M\xrightarrow{rN_m}M\to\cdots$.

Let $P(m)$ and $P(rm)$ be the resolutions from Step 1 and let $\pi: \mathbf Z[C_{rm}]\to\mathbf Z[C_m]$ be the induced ring map. Set $c_s=r^{\lfloor s/2\rfloor}$ and define $f_s=c_s\pi$. For $g'\in C_{rm}$ and $a\in\mathbf Z[C_{rm}]$, $f_s(g'a)=c_s\pi(g')\pi(a)=\pi(g')f_s(a)$, so $f_s$ is $\pi$-equivariant. Since $\pi(\sigma'-1)=\sigma-1$ and $\pi(N_{rm})=rN_m$, commutation with odd differentials is the equality $c_{2k}=c_{2k+1}$ and commutation with even differentials is $c_{2k+2}=rc_{2k+1}$; both hold. The degree-zero augmentation also commutes because $c_0=1$. Thus $f$ is a $\pi$-equivariant chain map lifting the identity of $\mathbf Z$.

Apply [lem-sfb-resolution-inflation-comparison] with $G=C_m$, $G'=C_{rm}$, the quotient $\pi$, and the chain map from Step 2. Both complexes are projective resolutions by [lem-sfb-cyclic-periodic-resolution], and Step 2 verifies the required augmentation equation. A cochain corresponding to $x\in M$ is the module map $h_x$ with $h_x(1)=x$. Precomposition sends it to $h_x\circ f_s$, whose value at $1$ is $h_x(c_s\pi(1))=c_sx$. Hence a source cocycle represented by $x$ is sent to the target cocycle represented by $r^{\lfloor s/2\rfloor}x$; this is the asserted formula for inflation.
If $rM=0$ and $s\geq2$, then $\lfloor s/2\rfloor\geq1$, so multiplication by $r^{\lfloor s/2\rfloor}$ is zero on $M$ and hence on the cohomology groups.
